turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: Bimala asked Sandip what was the truth behind the claims of oppression against Nikhil's tenantry, her voice calm and inquiring.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Nikhil told Sandip that his words to Bimala had only confirmed his suspicions of Sandip's tyranny and that he would not hesitate to take action if he continued to oppress his tenantry.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Nikhil asked Sandip to clarify what he meant by his previous statement, and to provide evidence of the oppression he had claimed to be suffering at Nikhil's hands.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Sandip told Bimala that Nikhil was as skilled at weaving lies as he was at collecting taxes, and that he should not be taken seriously.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Sandip said that Nikhil's warnings were as futile as a storm that fails to bring rain, and that he should not waste his breath on threats.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Sandip laughed and said that Nikhil's warnings were as credible as a thief's promise to return stolen goods, and that he should save his breath for more convincing lies

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Sandip said that Nikhil was so obsessed with his own importance that he had lost sight of reality, and that his warnings were nothing more than a desperate attempt to regain his lost stature.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Sandip asked Nikhil with a mocking grin, what else was new, more threats from the great Nikhil, the savior of the Zamindari family, and how did he plan to protect the villagers from his own incompetence.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Sandip said that Nikhil's warnings were as effective as a rusty sword, and that he should stop trying to frighten him with empty threats.

turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: Bimala asked Sandip, in a calm and neutral tone, what exactly Nikhil had warned him about, and what made him think the threat was so insignificant.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Nikhil told Sandip that his flippant attitude was a dereliction of duty, and that he should take the warnings seriously, for the safety of the villagers was not a matter to be trifled with

turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: Bimala asked Nikhil what evidence he had to support his warnings, and whether there were any tangible reasons to believe the local Mussulmans were planning an attack.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Nikhil insisted that the threat was not merely an empty boast, but a warning based on reliable intelligence gathered from trusted sources.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Nikhil told Bimala that the evidence he had gathered was too sensitive to be shared in public, but that she, as his wife and trusted advisor, should know the gravity of the situation.

turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: Bimala asked Nikhil if his intelligence network was reliable, and if he had considered the possibility of a miscommunication or misunderstanding

turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: Bimala asked Nikhil if he had considered the possibility of a misunderstanding arising from a cultural or linguistic misinterpretation.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Nikhil told Sandip that he would not engage in a futile debate with him, but urged him to take the threat seriously and prepare his estate accordingly.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Nikhil warned Bimala that the Mussulmans were not to be underestimated, and that their enmity towards their Hindu neighbors was a deep-seated one, passed down through generations.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Nikhil pointed to the recent uprisings in neighboring villages, emphasizing that the situation was grim and demanded attention.

turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: Bimala asked Nikhil if he had any evidence or concrete reasons to support his claims of a deep-seated enmity between the Mussulmans and the Hindus.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Sandip asked Bimala where she would go, addressing her as the Queen.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Sandip asked Nikhil if he kept Browning among his books, reminding him of a contest they had over translating lines from Browning, and inquiring if Nikhil remembered it.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Sandip told Nikhil and Bimala that he had managed to translate the lines into Bengali, but the result was unlikely to be well-received, and that he had once thought he was on the verge of becoming a poet, but Providence had intervened to prevent it, and he recalled old Dakshina's poetry.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Sandip told Bimala that it was pointless to search the bookshelves, as Nikhil no longer read poetry since his marriage, but that he, Sandip, was about to be afflicted with the 'fever fit of poesy' again.

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: Nikhil warned Sandip that he had come to give him a warning.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Sandip asked Nikhil if he was warning him about the 'fever fit of poesy'.

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: Nikhil told Sandip that for some time, Mahomedan preachers had been stirring up the local Mussulmans, who were angry with Sandip and might attack him at any moment.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Sandip asked Nikhil if he had come to advise him to flee.

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: Nikhil told Sandip that he had come to give him information, not advice.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Sandip told Nikhil that if the estates were his, a warning would have been necessary for the preachers, not for him, and that Nikhil should intimidate the preachers instead of frightening him, and that Nikhil's weakness was also affecting his neighbouring zamindars.

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: Nikhil told Sandip that he had not offered him advice, and that he wished Sandip would refrain from giving him his advice, as it was useless, and that there was another thing he wanted to tell Sandip, namely that Sandip and his followers had been secretly oppressing Nikhil's tenantry, and that he could no longer allow that, so he must ask Sandip to leave his territory.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Sandip asked Nikhil if he was threatening him with fear of the Mussulmans, or if there was another fear he had to threaten him with.
